question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to complete the idiom in the given sentence.**

I have been ________ over the two options in my head and I think we should go with the first one.
solution:
Here, the correct answer is "mulling."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
__
 
• **"Mulling over"** means to think carefully and at length about something, considering various aspects or options. (किसी चीज़ के बारे में सावधानीपूर्वक और गहराई से सोचना, विशेषकर निर्णय लेने से पहले)
 
• It fits well in the context of considering options before making a decision.
 
 
• **Example**: *She's been **mulling over**__ her decision for days.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 ​

Correct sentence:* **I have been __**mulling**__ over the two options in my head and I think we should go with the first one. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Seeing over: "Seeing over"** doesn't have a specific common meaning in English. It could be interpreted as overseeing or supervising something, but this usage is not very common. (किसी चीज़ की देखरेख करना)
 
• **Looking over: **examining or inspecting something with the intention of assessing its condition, details, or contents. (किसी चीज़ की स्थिति, विवरण या सामग्री का आकलन करने के इरादे से उसकी जांच या निरीक्षण करना)
 
• **Obsessing over: **becoming excessively preoccupied or fixated on something to the point where it dominates one's thoughts or actions. (किसी चीज़ पर इस हद तक अत्यधिक व्यस्त या केंद्रित हो जाना कि वह किसी के विचारों या कार्यों पर हावी हो जाए)
